prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear you were hurt — that’s stressful. I can’t pick one specific lawyer for you, but I can help you choose the right one and walk you through next steps in Pleasanton, CA.

Quick priorities
- Get medical care and follow treatment — medical records are critical.
- Preserve evidence (photos, vehicle damage, witness contact info, police report).
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the other party’s insurer or sign releases without a lawyer.
- California deadlines: generally 2 years from the injury to file a personal‑injury lawsuit (shorter rules apply for claims against a government entity — usually 6 months to file an administrative claim). Act early.

Which lawyer to look for
- Specialization: a lawyer who focuses mainly on motor vehicle accidents/personal injury (not a generalist).
- Experience with similar cases and with local courts (Alameda County judges, local insurers).
- Trial experience — many cases settle, but you want someone ready to litigate if needed.
- Good communication: responsive, explains strategy and timelines.
- Contingency-fee practice (no upfront fee; attorney paid from settlement/judgment). Ask exactly how fees and costs are handled.

How to compare lawyers (interview questions)
- Do you handle car-accident/personal-injury cases full time? How many per year?
- What was a recent case like mine you handled and what was the result?
- What percentage of your cases settle vs. go to trial?
- Who will work on my case (attorney vs. paralegal) and how will I contact them?
- What are your fees and costs? What percentage if settled before/after suit?
- Do you advance litigation costs or will I need to pay out-of-pocket?
- How long do you expect my case will take?
- What is your estimate of value/range, and why?

What to bring to a free consultation
- Police report number, photos of the scene/injuries, vehicle repair estimates.
- Medical records and bills, doctors’ notes, diagnosis.
- Insurance information (yours and the other party’s) and adjuster contact info.
- Any correspondence with insurers or the other party.
- Names/contact of witnesses.

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount.
- High-pressure “sign this today” tactics.
- Poor reviews about responsiveness or billing surprises.
- Lawyer unwilling to put fee agreement in writing.

Where to find attorneys in Pleasanton
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service.
- California State Bar “Find a Lawyer” website (check discipline status).
- Reviews on Google, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Yelp — read several reviews.
- Ask friends/family or other local professionals for referrals.

Fees and typical ranges
- Contingency fees often around 33% for pre‑lawsuit settlements, 33–40% if suit filed, sometimes higher if appeal/trial. Confirm exact terms in writing and any additional costs.

Legal points specific to CA
- California uses pure comparative negligence: you can recover even if partly at fault; damages are reduced by your percentage of fault.
- Statute of limitations: generally 2 years for personal injury claims; file earlier when a government entity is involved (often 6 months to file a claim).
- Preserve evidence immediately (photos, records, car repairs).

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft an email or script to use when contacting lawyers.
- Prepare a shortlist of things to check in online reviews and fee agreements.
- If you want me to look up local lawyers, tell me whether you want large firm vs. solo, language needs, or maximum travel distance and I’ll assemble a short list you can vet. (I’ll need permission to perform a web search or you can paste names you’ve found and I’ll help evaluate them.)

Do you want help preparing questions or composing messages to reach out to 3–5 attorneys for consultations? If so, tell me: date of accident, severity of injuries, whether police report exists, and whether you’ve already been contacted by an insurer.
